sentences.text:
Monish Nair vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:12114
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal

On The 11 th Of March, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 1162 of 2025
 Monish Nair
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Anurag Gohil - advocate for the applicant.
Ms. Sunita Sood - Panel Lawyer for State.

Order 
This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS/439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 137/2024 registered at Police Station - Misrod, District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC.
Applicant is in detention since 29.09.2024.
Previous bail application was dismissed as withdrawn.

2. As per the prosecution story, it is alleged that applicant has committed fraud with complainant,
therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He is in custody since 29.09.2024.
It is submitted that transaction between the applicant and complainant has taken place in March, 2023.
Complainant herself mentioned in the FIR that she has received some amount from the applicant.
FIR has been lodged after delay of one year.
Applicant has been enlarged on bail in Crime No.386/2023 by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 05.07.2024 passed in MCRC No.23412/2024.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12114 2 MCRC-1162-2025 Charge sheet has been filed and trial will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant on the ground of one criminal antecedent.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.

Consequently, bail Monish Nair vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162771674/
1 application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

sentences.text: 6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
7. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
8. Certified copy as per rules.
